ios.desc:
Stackrover is a unique interactive manual, training app, and knowledge base for all JavaScript developers. Build your skills and gain insight while waiting for a lunch or during any dull moment. Ditch all your fears and achieve real mastery step by step. Get prepared for any task you are up to.
Let Javascript finally make sense!
No sign-up, no ads, no recurring fees. Works fully offline.

Key features:

• over 1700 JavaScript-related concepts, constructs, and API elements explained
• detailed yet straightforward descriptions, annotated code samples
• answers to hard questions, tips, warnings, reassurances, lists, and overviews
• Mission board for information related to your current work
• Cheatboard for information you are looking up frequently
• Study board for topics you want to study systematically
• personal notes inserted right into the content
• dynamically generated quizzes
• custom quizzes based on the topics present in your boards

Convenient details:

• memory aids for things that are notoriously hard to remember
• content fine-tuned for high-distraction environments
• Term browser for more curious investigations into topics of interest
• add topics to your Study board directly from a quiz
• links to other useful resources
• instant anonymous feedback to make Stackrover's content ever more useful
• user manual included

quotes.text:
Hi! I'm Ondrej and I am an independent developer.
I've always felt there was a need for a different kind of manual for the web technologies. Not another copy-and-paste cookbook, but rather a resource for the developer's mind. One that systematically explains how things work, what they are good for, how they relate to each other, what their pitfalls are – i.e. one that helps develop real mental models.
So I crafted one, covering most of JavaScript by now. It's named Stackrover, because the idea is that more technologies could be covered in the future if the concept thrives.

The project actually comprises four endeavours: 1) a novel design system / visual language tailored to the needs of such a manual; 2) a custom markup language and its compiler; 3) the manual itself written in the markup language; 4) an interactive UI built around the manual so that users can make the most of it.

All these parts were designed and iterated over together. The markup language supports not only the content structure, phrasing, and various visual elements, but also metadata for the interactive features such as quizzes, search, and advanced navigation; and process marks to keep track of work in progress, testing, and quality control. The compiler outputs HTML, JSON metadata, plus some reports. Well, have a look at a tiny sample of the markup:
